articleTitle: The effect of phase and amplitude errors in FM radar
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Time-Bandwidth Product Waveforms in Radar and Sonar
abstract: Shows that the constraints on phase and amplitude errors derived for pulse compression radars (Klauder et al., 1960) should be applied with circumspection to FM radars, and in certain cases are actually unduly pessimistic.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pilot-an example of advanced FMCW techniques
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Time-Bandwidth Product Waveforms in Radar and Sonar
abstract: 'Pilot' is an FMCW tactical navigational radar which uses the high time-bandwidth product of frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) to provide excellent low probability of intercept (LPI) characteristics. It is shown that single antenna FMCW operation is feasible and practical and that FMCW MTI (moving target indication) can be implemented efficiently by using a correlation receiver.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The implementation of high time bandwidth chirp pulses using digital techniques
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Time-Bandwidth Product Waveforms in Radar and Sonar
abstract: Presents the design and development of the initial DCG (digital chirp generator), the current development program and a discussion of possible applications including spaceborne radar systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the application of the Fermat number transforms to the calculation of convolutions and correlations
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Time-Bandwidth Product Waveforms in Radar and Sonar
abstract: The Fermat number transform (FNT) has proved to be one of the most practical number theoretic transforms. The authors investigate the application of this transform to the calculation of convolutions and correlations with emphasis on the transform length constraints. Some techniques are introduced to increase the sequence length to be convolved through a fixed length (e.g. multiplierless) FNT while preserving other advantages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Extension of SAW pulse compression capability (radar systems)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Time-Bandwidth Product Waveforms in Radar and Sonar
abstract: The performance of SAW pulse compression radar systems can be appreciably enhanced by the use of digital waveform generators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparison of ambiguity surface performance and multiple access capacity for PSK and FH spread spectrum waveforms
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Time-Bandwidth Product Waveforms in Radar and Sonar
abstract: Examines auto- and cross-ambiguity surface performance of phase shift keyed (PSK) and frequency hopped (FH) waveforms in the presence of Doppler shifted received signals. A review of the design of various wideband signal coding techniques such as pseudo-noise (PN) and frequency hopped transmission for use in radar and communication systems is presented. Wideband coding of pulsed radar signals is used for protection against intentional interference. Alternatively the technique can be used to provide individual radars with a multiple access capability for simultaneous operation in a given frequency band. In radar, and also in mobile communication it is necessary to study the ambiguity surface to evaluate the performance under various Doppler frequency returns.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Time-Bandwidth Product Waveforms in Radar and Sonar
abstract: PRC (pseudo-random code) radar systems are being investigated for short range sensors and terminally guided submunitions (TGSM). A PRC radar system is presented which offers high resolution range and Doppler processing, and the simplicity of a solid state transceiver. System modelling has been used to predict system performance, and to identify the most critical parameters for code performance. A correlator ASIC has been designed using gallium arsenide technology, and 32 range bins have been incorporated onto this single chip, which should be capable of running at clock speeds greater than the required 167 MHz, allowing future updates when technology permits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A prototype FMCW radar using an analogue linear frequency sweep
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Time-Bandwidth Product Waveforms in Radar and Sonar
abstract: Describes a prototype FMCW radar system in which a phase-locked oscillator is used to generate the linear frequency sweep. Preliminary results show that the radar system is suitable for measurements of the Doppler spectra of echoes from water waves.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital expanders and compressors provide a cost effective solution for multi-pulse length radars
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Time-Bandwidth Product Waveforms in Radar and Sonar
abstract: Describes some aspects of modern radar design and the requirement for multiple pulse lengths. The author also describes a digital pulse compression system and its application to a surveillance radar and shows that it compares favourably against a SAW solution on technical and cost grounds.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Time-Bandwidth Product Waveforms in Radar and Sonar
abstract: The prototype system, designed to be suitable for a number of sonar transmitters, had two channels on a eurocard but recently a new version has been built using surface mounting and it has been possible to accommodate eight channels on each card. This board has also been interfaced to a PC which has allowed simple program development in Quick Basic. Examples of the wide range of possible waveforms are illustrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High performance time compression systems using fast frequency-domain correlation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Time-Bandwidth Product Waveforms in Radar and Sonar
abstract: Correlation processing for active sonar systems is discussed. The systems described use 32-bit complex vector processor (CVP) ASIC, high-speed dual port memory and a writable control store architecture to provide sustained data throughputs up to 25 million correlation points per second. This is sufficient for many sonar (and indeed some radar) applications. Two basic systems are outlined, one a single 6U PCB system using a single CVP for lower throughput systems, the other a two board, 8 CVP systolic pipeline processor supporting throughputs up to 25 million correlation points per second.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
